title: Person-by-Person 1 Chronicles, Second Temple High Priests, Hasmoneans, Herodians, Complete NT Apostles & Josephus

nodes.name: Hezron → Jerahmeel, Ram, Caleb (Chelubai) & Ashhur
nodes.role: Founders of the Four Great Clans of Judah
nodes.notes: Hezron (son of Perez) fathers Jerahmeel, Ram (ancestral line to David via Amminadab -> Nahshon -> Salmon + Rahab -> Boaz), Caleb/Chelubai (+ Azubah, Jerioth, Ephrath -> Hur), and posthumously Ashhur (father of Tekoa via Abijah).

nodes.name: Hur (son of Caleb & Ephrath) → Uri → Bezalel (Tabernacle Architect)
nodes.role: Chief Craftsman of the Ark & Tabernacle
nodes.notes: Hur (who held up Moses's hands at Rephidim alongside Aaron) fathers Uri -> Bezalel, Shobal (father of Kiriath-jearim), Salma (father of Bethlehem), and Hareph (father of Beth-gader).

nodes.name: Elimelech & Naomi → Mahlon (+ Ruth) & Chilion (+ Orpah)
nodes.role: Bethlehem Ephrathite Family of Ruth
nodes.notes: Elimelech and Naomi migrate from Bethlehem to Moab; their sons Mahlon and Chilion marry Moabite women Ruth and Orpah. After Mahlon's death, Boaz redeems Ruth, fathering Obed -> Jesse -> King David.

nodes.name: Jesse & Nitzevet → Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem & David
nodes.role: Complete Household of Jesse of Bethlehem
nodes.notes: Talmudic tradition names David's mother Nitzevet bat Adael. Jesse's seven sons (Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea/Shammah -> Jonadab, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, David) and two daughters (Zeruiah -> Joab/Abishai/Asahel; Abigail + Ithra/Jether -> Amasa).

nodes.name: King David's Jerusalem Nursery & Wives Registry (2 Sam 5:13; 1 Chr 3:5–9)
nodes.role: Structural Anchor for David's 20+ Named Children in Hebron & Jerusalem
nodes.notes: Structural court anchor uniting King David's Hebron sons (Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream) and Jerusalem sons (Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet II) plus daughters Tamar & Jerimoth's line.

nodes.name: Eliab (Reuben) → Nemuel, Dathan & Abiram (Korah's Rebellion)
nodes.role: Reubenite Leaders of the Wilderness Revolt
nodes.notes: Pallu -> Eliab -> Dathan and Abiram, who joined Korah the Levite in challenging Moses and Aaron in the wilderness. Also Reubenite Prince Elizur son of Shedeur & Shammua son of Zaccur (spy).

nodes.name: 24 Levitical Priestly Courses (Jehoiarib, Abijah, Zadok) & Temple Musicians
nodes.role: 24 Priestly Divisions + Asaph, Heman & Ethan (Jeduthun)
nodes.notes: King David organized Aaron's descendants (16 courses of Eleazar, 8 of Ithamar) into 24 priestly rotations: 1. Jehoiarib (Hasmonean/Maccabee clan!), 8. Abijah (Zechariah father of John the Baptist!). Alongside Temple Choirs of Gershon (Asaph), Kohath (Heman), and Merari (Ethan/Jeduthun).

nodes.name: Machir (Manasseh) → Gilead → Hepher → Zelophehad & Jair
nodes.role: Transjordanian House of Manasseh
nodes.notes: Machir (son of Manasseh & an Aramean concubine) -> Gilead -> Iezer (ancestor of Gideon!), Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher -> Zelophehad (whose 5 daughters Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, Tirzah established female inheritance law in Israel!).

nodes.name: Ephraim → Beriah & Sherah → Resheph → Elishama → Nun → Joshua
nodes.role: Complete 10-Generation Ephraimite Lineage to Joshua
nodes.notes: 1 Chronicles 7 records Ephraim's daughter Sherah (who built Lower & Upper Beth-horon!) and traces Beriah -> Rephah -> Resheph -> Telah -> Tahan -> Ladan -> Ammihud -> Elishama (Prince of Ephraim) -> Nun -> Joshua (Yehoshua).

nodes.name: Jeiel / Abiel → Ner → General Abner & Kish → King Saul's Sons
nodes.role: Complete Benjamite Royal House of Saul
nodes.notes: Abiel fathers Kish (father of King Saul) and Ner (father of General Abner, commander of Saul's army). Saul's sons: Jonathan (-> Mephibosheth -> Mica), Abinadab, Malchishua, Ish-bosheth (Eshbaal), plus Armoni & Mephibosheth (by Rizpah bat Aiah), and daughters Merab & Michal.

nodes.name: Jeroboam I & Queen Ano (Egyptian Princess) → Abijah & Nadab
nodes.role: Egyptian Royal Marriage of Israel's First Northern King
nodes.notes: The Greek Septuagint preserves the name Ano, sister-in-law of Pharaoh Shishak (Shoshenq I), given in marriage to Jeroboam I during his Egyptian exile — linking the Northern Kingdom of Israel directly to Egypt's 22nd Dynasty!

nodes.name: 8 Early Kings of Edom (Bela ben Beor through Hadar & Queen Mehetabel)
nodes.role: Elective Pre-Israelite Kings of Edom
nodes.notes: Eight kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over Israel: 1. Bela ben Beor (Dinhabah), 2. Jobab ben Zerah of Bozrah, 3. Husham (Temanites), 4. Hadad ben Bedad (defeated Midian), 5. Samlah (Masrekah), 6. Shaul (Rehoboth), 7. Baal-hanan ben Achbor, 8. Hadar/Hadad (+ Mehetabel bat Matred).

nodes.name: Post-Exilic High Priestly Restoration Covenant (Jeshua → Jaddua)
nodes.role: Persian-Era Zadokite Restoration Hub
nodes.notes: Restoration of the Zadokite High Priesthood at the Second Temple from Jeshua ben Jehozadak down to Jaddua.

nodes.name: Oniad High Priestly Covenant (Alexandria & Leontopolis Branch)
nodes.role: Hellenistic-Era Oniad Branch of the Zadokite Line
nodes.notes: Hellenistic branch of High Priest Jaddua's house spanning Onias I through Onias IV's Temple at Leontopolis in Egypt.

nodes.name: Mattathias of Modi'in (Priest of Course of Jehoiarib)
nodes.era: c. 167 BCE (1 Macc 2; Josephus Ant. XII.6)
nodes.role: Patriarch of the Maccabean Revolt
nodes.notes: Priest of the line of Joarib/Jehoiarib (son of John, son of Simeon, son of Asamonaeus/Hasmon) who sparked the revolt against Seleucid King Antiochus IV Epiphanes. Father of 5 sons: John Gaddi, Simon Thassi, Judas Maccabeus, Eleazar Avaran, and Jonathan Apphus.

nodes.name: Judas Maccabeus ('The Hammer')
nodes.role: Third Son of Mattathias & Hanukkah Liberator
nodes.notes: Third son of Mattathias who defeated Seleucid armies and rededicated the Second Temple in 164 BCE (origin of Hanukkah).

nodes.name: Judas ben Simon Thassi (Slain at Dok, 1 Macc 16:14)
nodes.era: c. 160-135 BCE (1 Macc 16; Josephus Ant. XIII.7)
nodes.role: Son of Simon Thassi & Brother of John Hyrcanus I
nodes.notes: Son of Ethnarch Simon Thassi assassinated alongside his father and brother Mattathias at Dok by Ptolemy son of Abubus while brother John Hyrcanus escaped to succeed as Ethnarch.

nodes.name: Antigonus I (Son of John Hyrcanus I)
nodes.role: Hasmonean Prince & Military Commander
nodes.notes: Younger brother of King Aristobulus I and co-victor at Samaria who was assassinated at Strato's Tower before Alexander Jannaeus assumed the throne.

nodes.name: Alexandra the Maccabee (Daughter of Hyrcanus II)
nodes.role: Hasmonean Princess & Mother of Queen Mariamne I
nodes.notes: Daughter of High Priest Hyrcanus II who married her cousin Alexander II (son of King Aristobulus II), bearing Queen Mariamne I (wife of Herod the Great) and High Priest Aristobulus III.

nodes.name: Antipater I the Idumean (Procurator of Judea, d. 43 BCE)
nodes.role: Idumean Founder of the Herodian House
nodes.notes: Son of Antipas (governor of Idumea); appointed Procurator of Judea by Julius Caesar; married Nabataean princess Cypros and fathered Phasael I, Herod I the Great, Joseph I, Pheroras, and Salome I.

nodes.name: King Herod I the Great (37-4 BCE)
nodes.role: Roman Client King of Judea & Builder of the Second Temple
nodes.notes: Son of Antipater I & Cypros; married ten wives (Doris, Hasmonean Mariamne I, Mariamne II, Malthace, Cleopatra of Jerusalem, Pallas, Phaedra, Elpis, niece, cousin) and fathered Antipater II, Alexander, Aristobulus IV, Herod II Philip, Archelaus, Antipas, and Philip the Tetrarch.

nodes.name: Berenice I (Daughter of Salome I; Wife of Aristobulus IV)
nodes.role: Mother of King Herod Agrippa I, Herod of Chalcis & Herodias
nodes.notes: Daughter of Herod's sister Salome I and Costobarus; married Prince Aristobulus IV, birthing King Herod Agrippa I, King Herod of Chalcis, Aristobulus Minor, Herodias, and Mariamne III.

nodes.name: Joachim / Heli (Maternal Grandfather of Jesus)
nodes.role: Father of the Virgin Mary
nodes.notes: Early Christian tradition (Protoevangelium of James) names Mary's father Joachim (harmonized with Heli in Luke 3:23) and her mother Saint Anne.

nodes.name: Clopas / Alphaeus (Brother of Joseph of Nazareth)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Matt 10:3; John 19:25; Eusebius HE III.11)
nodes.role: Holy Family Kinsman & Husband of Mary of Clopas
nodes.notes: Hegesippus (in Eusebius) records Clopas as brother of Joseph of Nazareth; husband of Mary of Clopas and father of Bishop Simeon of Jerusalem, Apostle James the Lesser, and Jude Thaddeus.

nodes.name: Zebedee of Galilee (Father of James & John)
nodes.role: Galilean Fisherman & Father of the 'Sons of Thunder'
nodes.notes: Husband of Salome (Mark 15:40; Matt 27:56) and father of inner-circle Apostles James the Great and John the Evangelist.

nodes.name: Jonah / John of Bethsaida (Father of Simon Peter & Andrew)
nodes.role: Father of Chief Apostles Simon Peter & Andrew
nodes.notes: Named in Matthew 16:17 (Bar-Jonah) and John 1:42 as father of Galilean fisherman brothers Simon Peter and Andrew.

nodes.name: Apostolic College of the Twelve & 1st-Century Church
nodes.role: Core Discipleship Network Around Jesus of Nazareth
nodes.notes: Structural hub uniting the Twelve Apostles (Simon Peter, Andrew, James the Great, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the Lesser, Jude Thaddeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas Iscariot, and Matthias).

nodes.name: Mary of Jerusalem (Mother of John Mark; Cousin of Barnabas)
nodes.role: Matriarch of the Upper Room Church Household in Jerusalem
nodes.notes: Hosted the Jerusalem church in her house (Acts 12:12); mother of Evangelist John Mark and kinswoman of Levite Barnabas of Cyprus.

nodes.name: Josephus's Table of Nations Key (Gomer=Gauls, Magog=Scythians, Tubal=Iberians, Meshech=Cappadocians, Tiras=Thracians)
nodes.role: Earliest Classical Greek-to-Genesis Ethnographic Key
nodes.notes: Flavius Josephus systematically mapped Genesis 10 into 1st-century Greco-Roman geography: Gomer=Galatians/Gauls, Magog=Scythians, Madai=Medes, Javan=Ionians/Greeks, Tubal=Iberes, Meshech=Cappadocians (Mazaca), Tiras=Thracians, Ashkenaz=Rheginians, Riphath=Paphlagonians, Togarmah=Phrygians, Elishah=Aeolians, Tarshish=Cilicia (Tarsus), Kittim=Cyprus (Kition).

nodes.name: Syriac Antediluvian Matriarchs: Lebhûdhâ (Cain's Twin/Wife), Ķelîmath/Aklia (Abel's Twin, Seth's Wife) & Haykêl bat Namûs (Noah's Wife)
nodes.era: Antediluvian Syriac Tradition (Cave of Treasures pp. 69-100, 197-198)
nodes.role: Complete Syriac Matriarchal Chain from Eve to Noah's Wife Haykêl
nodes.notes: Names every matriarch across 10 antediluvian generations: Cain + twin Lebhûdhâ; Seth + Ķelîmath (Abel's twin); Enos + Ḥannâ; Cainan + Peryath; Mahalalel + Şeḥatpar; Jared + Zebhîdhâ; Enoch + Zadhkîn; Methuselah + Sâkhûth; Lamech + Kîpâr; Noah + Haykêl (daughter of Namûs)! Also names Terah's 2 wives: Yônâ (mother of Abraham) & Salmûth (mother of Sarah).

nodes.name: Yonton / Jonitus (Yônṭôn — 4th Son of Noah)
nodes.era: Post-Flood East (Cave of Treasures pp. 122, 143-144; Bar Hebraeus)
nodes.role: Post-Diluvian 4th Son of Noah & Origin of Eastern Wisdom
nodes.notes: Born to Noah after the Flood and sent east to Yôkdôrâ of Nôdh by Lake Aṭrâs ('Land of the Rising Sun'). Nimrod journeyed east to Yonton (Jonitus) for 3 years and received the astronomical 'Revelation (Gelyânâ) of Nimrod' — the star-prophecy later followed by the Magi to Bethlehem!

nodes.name: Syriac Melchizedek Lineage: Mâlâkh (son of Arphaxad/Cainan) & Yôzâdhâk → Melchizedek
nodes.role: Syriac Parentage of Melchizedek & Guardian of Adam's Body at Golgotha
nodes.notes: Unlike rabbinic Shem=Melchizedek, the Syriac Cave of Treasures names Melchizedek's parents as Mâlâkh (brother of Salah, grandson of Arphaxad) and Yôzâdhâk (Book of the Bee variant: Harklêîm & Shêlâthîêl). Shem led 15-year-old Melchizedek to entomb Adam's body at Golgotha!

nodes.name: Syriac Twin Fathers of Joseph & Mary: Matthan + Sebhrath → Twins Jacob (→ Joseph) & Yônâkhîr (+ Dînâ/Ḥannâ → Mary)
nodes.role: Syriac Harmonization Making Joseph & Virgin Mary First Cousins!
nodes.notes: Preserves EVERY post-exilic matriarch from Zerubbabel (+ Malkath bat Ezra!) through Abiud (+ Zakhyath bat Joshua) to Matthan (+ Sebhrath bat Phinehas), who bore TWINS Jacob (father of Joseph by Ḥadbhîth) and Yônâkhîr (father of Mary by Dînâ/Ḥannâ)!

nodes.name: The Magi Kings of the East: Hôrmîzdâdh (Persia), Îzgarad (Sâbhâ) & Perôzadh (Sheba) + 12 Magi (Book of the Bee)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Cave of Treasures pp. 208-209; Book of the Bee Ch. 39)
nodes.role: Persian & Sabaean Royal Astronomers Following Nimrod's Prophecy to Christ
nodes.notes: Three kings: Hôrmîzdâdh of Mâkhôzdî (King of Kings of Persia), Îzgarad (Yazdegerd, King of Sâbhâ), and Perôzadh (King of Sheba). Book of the Bee expands to 12 named Magi with patronymics (Zarwândâd s/o Artabân, Gûshnâsâph s/o Gûndaphar [Indo-Parthian Gondophares!], Arshakh, Merôdâch, etc.)!

nodes.name: First Temple High Priests (Dutripon p. 23, #4–34): Abishua → Bukki → Uzzi → Zadok → Ahimaaz → Jehoiada → Hilkiah → Seraiah
nodes.role: Complete Pre-Exilic High Priestly Succession from Aaron to the Babylonian Exile
nodes.notes: Dutripon's Tabula Pontificum apud Judaeos harmonizes Chronicles, Josephus & Eusebius across all 34 pre-exilic High Priests, including Jehoiada (who sheltered young King Joash from Queen Athaliah) and Hilkiah (who discovered the Book of the Law under King Josiah).

nodes.name: Herodian & Roman-Era High Priests (Dutripon p. 23, #63–91): Ananelus → Simon ben Boethus → Annas (Ananus) → Joseph Caiaphas → Ananias ben Nebedeus → Ananus II → Phannias (70 CE)
nodes.era: 37 BCE – 70 CE (Dutripon Concordantiae p. 23; Gospels; Acts 23; Josephus Ant. XV-XX)
nodes.role: Complete Final 29 High Priests of the Second Temple Down to the Fall of Jerusalem (70 CE)
nodes.notes: Complete chronological table from Herod's appointee Ananelus & Simon ben Boethus (Herod's father-in-law) through Annas (Ananus) and son-in-law Joseph Caiaphas (Trial of Jesus), Annas's 5 High Priest sons (Eleazar, Jonathan, Theophilus, Matthias, Ananus II — who executed James the Just in 62 CE!), Ananias ben Nebedeus (Trial of Paul, Acts 23), down to Phannias/Phanacius, the VERY LAST High Priest chosen by lot during the 70 CE siege!

nodes.name: 11 Territorial Dukes of Esau (Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel, Iram) & Jobab = Job Bridge
nodes.role: Final Edomite Chiefs & Septuagint/Vulgate Identification of King Jobab with Patriarch Job
nodes.notes: Dutripon's Series Principum Regumque Idumaeorum explicitly records the ancient Septuagint/Vulgate tradition ('Jobab iste est Job speculum patientiae') identifying Edomite King #2 Jobab ben Zerah of Bozrah with the Biblical Patriarch Job, followed by the 11 territorial Dukes of Edom.

nodes.name: Deuterocanonical & Vulgate Households (Dutripon pp. 10-15): Tobit & Tobias (+ Sarah bat Raguel), Judith of Bethulia, Susanna, Eleazar & 7 Maccabean Martyrs, Ben Sira & Prophetesses Huldah & Anna
nodes.era: c. 744 BCE – 1 CE (Dutripon Index Chronologicus pp. 10-15)
nodes.role: Biblical & Intertestamental Families Preserved in the Latin Vulgate Chronology
sources: Books of Tobit, Judith, Sirach, 2 Maccabees
nodes.notes: Tobit (Tribe of Naphtali, exiled to Nineveh under Shalmaneser) -> Tobias (+ Sarah daughter of Raguel); Widow Judith of Bethulia (slew General Holofernes); Susanna (vindicated by Daniel); Eleazar & 7 Maccabean Martyrs (168 BCE); Jesus ben Sirach (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus, translated in Alexandria 131 BCE); Prophetess Huldah (Josiah's reign) & Prophetess Anna bat Phanuel (Tribe of Asher, Temple of Jerusalem!).

nodes.name: Intersecting Ancient Near Eastern Kings in Dutripon's Sacred Chronology (pp. 9-14): Chedorlaomer of Elam, Sihon & Og of Bashan, Cushan-Rishathaim, Eglon of Moab, Jabin & Sisera, Zerah the Cushite & Tibni
nodes.era: c. 1949-880 BCE (Dutripon pp. 9-14; Gen 14; Num 21; Judges 3-4; 2 Chr 14)
nodes.role: Foreign Kings & Rivals Synchronized Across Dutripon's Six Ages of the World
nodes.notes: Key intersecting monarchs in Dutripon's Six Ages tables: Chedorlaomer of Elam (vs. Abraham, Gen 14), Amorite Kings Sihon & Og of Bashan (Num 21), Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram-Naharaim (vs. Othniel), Eglon of Moab (vs. Ehud), Jabin of Hazor & Sisera (vs. Deborah/Barak), Zerah the Cushite/Ethiopian (vs. King Asa, 2 Chr 14), and rival King Tibni of Israel (vs. Omri, 1 Kgs 16).

nodes.name: Dutripon's Vulgate Ethnographic & Onomastic Key (pp. 9-15, 24-26): Nimrod=Belus, Asshur=Ninus, Armenia=Ararat, Carthago=Tarshish, India=Ophir/Hodu, Greece=Javan, Libya=Lubim & Patriarch Etymologies
nodes.role: Classical Latin Vulgate Cross-Cultural Identifications & Hebrew/Chaldean/Greek Name Meanings
nodes.notes: Documents traditional Latin Vulgate & Ussher synchronisms: Nimrod=Belus, Asshur=Ninus (+ Semiramis & Ninyas), Aegialeus of Sicyon & Inachus of Argos, Ogygian Flood (1796 BC), Cecrops & Cadmus, PLUS pp. 24-26 Name Interpretations: Aethiopia=Chus, Africa=Phut, Alexandria=No-Ammon, Armenia=Ararat, Cappadoces=Caphthorim, Carthago=Tharsis, Graeci=Jevanim, Heliopolis=On, India=Ophir/Hodu, Libya=Lubim, Cyrus=Sun; Adam ('red earth'), Eva ('living'), Noe ('rest'), Abraham ('father of multitude'), Moyses ('drawn from water'), David ('beloved'), Jesus ('Savior').

nodes.notes: Son of Eliashib; grandfather of Manasseh of Gerizim and High Priest Jaddua.

nodes.name: High Priest Johanan / Jonathan ben Joiada (Neh 12:11, 22; Elephantine Papyri!)
nodes.role: Fifth Post-Exilic High Priest (Named in Elephantine Papyri)
nodes.notes: Son of Joiada; attested outside Scripture as 'Yehohanan the High Priest' in the 407 BCE Aramaic Elephantine Petition.

nodes.name: High Priest Jaddua (Met Alexander the Great, 332 BCE)
nodes.role: Sixth Post-Exilic High Priest Who Welcomed Alexander
nodes.notes: Son of Johanan; according to Josephus Ant. XI.8.5, met Alexander the Great at Sapha/Jerusalem in 332 BCE and showed him Daniel's prophecies.

nodes.name: Manasseh (Brother of Jaddua; Co-Founder of Samaritan Temple, Ant. XI.7–8)
nodes.role: Brother of High Priest Jaddua Married to Nicaso bat Sanballat
nodes.notes: Brother of High Priest Jaddua; wed Nicaso daughter of Cuthean governor Sanballat and became first priest of the Mount Gerizim temple under Alexander.

nodes.name: Nicaso (Daughter of Sanballat of Samaria; Wife of Manasseh, Ant. XI.7.2)
nodes.role: Daughter of Governor Sanballat
nodes.notes: Daughter of Sanballat who wed Zadokite priest Manasseh, sparking the Jerusalem–Gerizim priestly schism.

nodes.name: High Priest Onias I (Son of Jaddua, c. 320–290 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of the Oniad Line of High Priests
nodes.notes: Son of Jaddua; contemporary of Spartan King Areus I in Josephus Ant. XII.4.10.

nodes.name: High Priest Simon I the Just (c. 290–275 BCE, Sirach 50)
nodes.era: c. 290–275 BCE (Josephus Ant. XII.2.5; Pirkei Avot 1:2)
nodes.role: Celebrated Oniad High Priest ('Shimon ha-Tzaddik')
nodes.notes: Son of Onias I; celebrated for piety and integrity, leaving young son Onias II under his brother Eleazar's regency.

nodes.name: High Priest Eleazar (Brother of Simon I; Septuagint Sponsor)
nodes.era: c. 275–255 BCE (Letter of Aristeas; Josephus Ant. XII.2)
nodes.role: High Priest Who Dispatched the 72 Translators to Alexandria
nodes.notes: Brother of Simon I the Just; sent the 72 Torah elders from Jerusalem to King Ptolemy II Philadelphus to produce the Greek Septuagint.

nodes.name: High Priest Onias II (Son of Simon I; Uncle of Tobiad Joseph)
nodes.role: Son of Simon the Just
nodes.notes: Son of Simon I; his sister married Tobias, producing the Tobiad tax-farming dynasty.

nodes.name: High Priest Simon II (Son of Onias II, c. 220–196 BCE)
nodes.role: Father of Onias III, Jason & Menelaus
nodes.notes: Son of Onias II; praised in Ben Sira 50:1–21 for repairing and fortifying the Second Temple.

nodes.name: High Priest Onias III (Son of Simon II; Martyr c. 171 BCE)
nodes.era: c. 196–171 BCE (2 Macc 3–4; Josephus Ant. XII.5)
nodes.role: Righteous Last Jerusalem Oniad High Priest
nodes.notes: Son of Simon II; deposed by brother Jason and murdered at Daphne near Antioch while in exile.

nodes.name: High Priest Jason / Joshua (Son of Simon II; Hellenizer, 175–172 BCE)
nodes.role: Brother of Onias III Who Purchased the High Priesthood
nodes.notes: Brother of Onias III who outbid him with Antiochus IV Epiphanes and built a gymnasium in Jerusalem.

nodes.name: High Priest Onias IV (Son of Onias III; Founder of Leontopolis Temple, Egypt)
nodes.role: Builder of the Jewish Temple in Heliopolis/Leontopolis
nodes.notes: Son of Onias III; fled to Ptolemy VI Philometor and Cleopatra II in Egypt and built the Temple of Onias at Leontopolis; father of generals Helkias & Ananias.

nodes.name: General Helkias (Son of Onias IV; Commander Under Cleopatra III)
nodes.role: Oniad-Jewish Military Commander in Ptolemaic Egypt
nodes.notes: Son of Onias IV who defended Queen Cleopatra III and allied with Hasmonean King Alexander Jannaeus.

nodes.name: General Ananias (Son of Onias IV; Commander Under Cleopatra III)
nodes.role: Oniad-Jewish General Who Preserved Judean Independence
nodes.notes: Son of Onias IV who persuaded Queen Cleopatra III not to annex Judea against Alexander Jannaeus.

nodes.name: John Gaddi (Eldest Son of Mattathias, d. 160 BCE)
nodes.role: Firstborn Son of Mattathias of Modi'in
nodes.notes: Eldest of the five Maccabean brothers.

nodes.name: Simon Thassi (2nd Son of Mattathias; Ethnarch & High Priest 142–135 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of the Independent Hasmonean State
nodes.notes: Last surviving brother of Judas Maccabeus; won full independence from the Seleucids and sired Judas, Mattathias, and John Hyrcanus I.

nodes.name: Eleazar Avaran (4th Son of Mattathias, d. 162 BCE)
nodes.role: Fourth Son of Mattathias
nodes.notes: Heroically died beneath a Seleucid war elephant at Beth-zechariah.

nodes.name: Jonathan Apphus (5th Son of Mattathias; 1st Hasmonean High Priest 152–143 BCE)
nodes.role: First Hasmonean High Priest of Judea
nodes.notes: Succeeded Judas Maccabeus as commander and became the first Hasmonean High Priest.

nodes.name: Mattathias ben Simon Thassi (Slain at Dok, 1 Macc 16:14)
nodes.role: Younger Brother of John Hyrcanus I
nodes.notes: Son of Ethnarch Simon Thassi assassinated at Dok with his father and brother Judas.

nodes.name: John Hyrcanus I (Ethnarch & High Priest 134–104 BCE)
nodes.role: Son of Simon Thassi Who Conquered Idumea & Samaria
nodes.notes: Son of Simon Thassi; expanded Judea across Samaria and Idumea; father of Aristobulus I, Antigonus I, and Alexander Jannaeus.

nodes.name: King Aristobulus I / Judah (1st Hasmonean King, 104–103 BCE)
nodes.role: First Hasmonean to Take the Royal Diadem
nodes.notes: Eldest son of John Hyrcanus I and husband of Queen Salome Alexandra before his death.

nodes.name: King Alexander Jannaeus (103–76 BCE)
nodes.role: Hasmonean Warrior King & High Priest
nodes.notes: Third son of John Hyrcanus I; married widow Salome Alexandra and fathered Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II.

nodes.name: Queen Salome Alexandra (Regnant Queen of Judea, 76–67 BCE)
nodes.role: Sole Regnant Queen of the Hasmonean Dynasty
nodes.notes: Widow of Aristobulus I and Alexander Jannaeus who reigned independently over Judea during a Pharisaic golden age.

nodes.name: High Priest & Ethnarch Hyrcanus II (76–40 BCE, d. 30 BCE)
nodes.role: Elder Son of Alexander Jannaeus & Salome Alexandra
nodes.notes: High Priest and Ethnarch of Judea; father of Alexandra the Maccabee.

nodes.name: King Aristobulus II of Judea (67–63 BCE, d. 49 BCE)
nodes.role: Younger Son of Alexander Jannaeus & Salome Alexandra
nodes.notes: Contested the throne against brother Hyrcanus II until Pompey intervened in 63 BCE; father of Alexander II and Antigonus II.

nodes.name: Alexander II of Judea (Son of Aristobulus II, d. 49 BCE)
nodes.role: Husband of Cousin Alexandra & Father of Mariamne I
nodes.notes: Son of Aristobulus II; wed cousin Alexandra (daughter of Hyrcanus II), uniting the two rival Hasmonean branches in Mariamne I and Aristobulus III.

nodes.name: King Antigonus II Mattathias (Last Hasmonean King, 40–37 BCE)
nodes.role: Final Hasmonean Sovereign Executed at Antioch
nodes.notes: Younger son of Aristobulus II; reclaimed Jerusalem with Parthian aid before Herod and Rome captured him in 37 BCE.

nodes.name: Queen Mariamne I the Hasmonean (Wife 2 of Herod the Great, d. 29 BCE)
nodes.role: Hasmonean Princess Bridging the Maccabees & Herodians
nodes.notes: Daughter of Alexander II and Alexandra; married Herod the Great, bearing Prince Alexander, Prince Aristobulus IV, Salampsio, and Cypros — passing Hasmonean royal blood into Armenia, Cilicia & Rome.

nodes.name: High Priest Aristobulus III (Last Hasmonean High Priest, d. 36 BCE)
nodes.role: Brother of Queen Mariamne I Drowned at Jericho
nodes.notes: Brother of Queen Mariamne I; served briefly as High Priest at age 17 before Herod had him drowned.

nodes.name: Queen Cypros of Nabataea (Wife of Antipater I, Josephus Ant. XIV.7.3)
nodes.role: Nabataean Mother of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Nobly born Nabataean princess; wife of Antipater I and mother of Phasael I, Herod the Great, Joseph I, Pheroras, and Salome I.

nodes.name: Phasael I (Eldest Son of Antipater I; Tetrarch of Jerusalem, d. 40 BCE)
nodes.role: Eldest Brother of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Joint tetrarch with Herod under Mark Antony; captured by Parthians and died honorably; father of Phasael II's namesake.

nodes.name: Joseph I (Brother of Herod the Great, d. 38 BCE)
nodes.role: Third Son of Antipater I & Cypros
nodes.notes: Brother and general of Herod the Great slain near Jericho fighting Antigonus II.

nodes.name: Pheroras (Tetrarch of Perea; Youngest Brother of Herod, d. 5 BCE)
nodes.role: Fourth Son of Antipater I & Cypros
nodes.notes: Appointed Tetrarch of Perea by Augustus; youngest son of Antipater I and Cypros.

nodes.name: Salome I (Sister of Herod the Great; Mother of Berenice I)
nodes.role: Sister of Herod & Wife of Costobarus
nodes.notes: Sister of Herod I; married Joseph, Costobarus (governor of Idumea & Gaza), and Alexas; mother of Berenice I.

nodes.name: Costobarus of Idumea (2nd Husband of Salome I; Father of Berenice I)
nodes.role: Idumean Governor Descended from Priests of Qos
nodes.notes: Hereditary Idumean noble; married Herod's sister Salome I and fathered Berenice I (grandmother of Herod Agrippa I).

nodes.name: Doris of Jerusalem (Wife 1 of Herod I; Mother of Antipater II)
nodes.role: First Wife of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Jewish noblewoman; Herod's first wife and mother of firstborn Antipater II.

nodes.name: Mariamne II (Daughter of High Priest Simon ben Boethus; Wife 3 of Herod)
nodes.role: Daughter of High Priest Simon ben Boethus
nodes.notes: Daughter of Alexandria-born High Priest Simon ben Boethus; wife 3 of Herod and mother of Herod II Philip.

nodes.name: Malthace of Samaria (Wife 4 of Herod; Mother of Archelaus, Antipas & Olympias)
nodes.role: Samaritan Wife of Herod & Mother of Rulers Archelaus & Antipas
nodes.notes: Samaritan wife of Herod the Great who bore Ethnarch Archelaus, Tetrarch Herod Antipas, and Princess Olympias.

nodes.name: Cleopatra of Jerusalem (Wife 5 of Herod; Mother of Philip the Tetrarch)
nodes.role: Wife 5 of Herod & Mother of Tetrarch Philip II
nodes.notes: Mother of Herod's son Herod and of Philip the Tetrarch of Iturea and Trachonitis (Luke 3:1).

nodes.name: Pallas (Wife 6 of Herod; Mother of Phasael II, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.role: Sixth Wife of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Sixth wife of Herod I; bore Phasael II.

nodes.name: Phaedra (Wife 7 of Herod; Mother of Roxane, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.role: Seventh Wife of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Seventh wife of Herod I; bore Princess Roxane.

nodes.name: Elpis (Wife 8 of Herod; Mother of Salome II, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.role: Eighth Wife of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Eighth wife of Herod I; bore Princess Salome II.

nodes.name: Antipater II (Firstborn Son of Herod & Doris, d. 4 BCE)
nodes.role: Eldest Son of Herod the Great
nodes.notes: Executed five days before Herod the Great's own death in 4 BCE.

nodes.name: Prince Alexander (Son of Herod & Queen Mariamne I, d. 7 BCE)
nodes.role: Hasmonean-Herodian Heir & Ancestor of Kings of Armenia
nodes.notes: Elder son of Herod I and Queen Mariamne I; married Princess Glaphyra of Cappadocia and fathered King Tigranes V of Armenia and Alexander II.

nodes.name: Princess Glaphyra of Cappadocia (Daughter of King Archelaus; Wife of Alexander & Juba II)
nodes.era: c. 35 BCE – 7 CE (Josephus Ant. XVI.1, XVII.13.4)
nodes.role: Cappadocian Royal Mother of the Herodian Kings of Armenia
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Archelaus of Cappadocia; wed Prince Alexander (son of Herod), King Juba II of Mauretania, and Ethnarch Archelaus.

nodes.name: Prince Aristobulus IV (Son of Herod & Mariamne I, d. 7 BCE)
nodes.role: Hasmonean-Herodian Prince & Father of Herod Agrippa I
nodes.notes: Younger son of Herod I and Mariamne I; wed Berenice I (daughter of Salome I) and fathered Herod Agrippa I, Herod of Chalcis, and Herodias.

nodes.name: Salampsio (Daughter of Herod & Mariamne I; Wife of Phasael II)
nodes.era: c. 30 BCE – 1st c. CE (Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.role: Daughter of Herod & Queen Mariamne I
nodes.notes: Married her cousin Phasael II; mother of Cypros (wife of Herod Agrippa I).

nodes.name: Cypros (Daughter of Herod & Mariamne I; Wife of Antipater s/o Salome I)
nodes.era: c. 29 BCE – 1st c. CE (Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.role: Daughter of Herod & Queen Mariamne I
nodes.notes: Younger sister of Alexander and Aristobulus IV by Queen Mariamne I.

nodes.name: Herod II / Herod Boethus (Son of Herod & Mariamne II; 1st Husband of Herodias)
nodes.era: c. 22 BCE – 33 CE (Matt 14:3; Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.1)
nodes.role: Son of Herod & High Priest Simon's Daughter Mariamne II
nodes.notes: Disinherited private citizen living in Rome/Jerusalem; first husband of niece Herodias and father of Princess Salome.

nodes.name: Ethnarch Herod Archelaus (Ruled Judea & Samaria 4 BCE–6 CE)
nodes.role: Son of Herod & Malthace; Ethnarch of Judea
nodes.notes: Inherited Judea, Samaria & Idumea under Augustus; deposed to Gaul in 6 CE.

nodes.name: Tetrarch Herod Antipas (Ruled Galilee 4 BCE–39 CE; Mark 6:14)
nodes.era: 20 BCE – after 39 CE (Luke 3:1, 23:7; Josephus Ant. XVIII)
nodes.role: Tetrarch of Galilee & Perea at Trial of Jesus & Execution of John the Baptist
nodes.notes: Son of Herod I & Malthace; wed Phasaelis (daughter of Aretas IV of Nabataea) and later niece-sister-in-law Herodias.

nodes.name: Princess Olympias (Daughter of Herod & Malthace, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.role: Daughter of Herod & Malthace
nodes.notes: Married cousin Joseph (son of Joseph I) and bore Mariamne (wife of Herod of Chalcis).

nodes.name: Tetrarch Philip II (Ruled Iturea & Trachonitis 4 BCE–34 CE; Builder of Caesarea Philippi)
nodes.era: c. 20 BCE – 34 CE (Luke 3:1; Josephus Ant. XVIII.4.6)
nodes.role: Son of Herod & Cleopatra of Jerusalem; Husband of Salome
nodes.notes: Just tetrarch of northeast Galilee/Golan who wed Princess Salome (daughter of Herodias); died childless in 34 CE.

nodes.name: Roxane (Daughter of Herod I & Phaedra, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.role: Daughter of Herod I & Phaedra
nodes.notes: Married a son of Herod's brother Pheroras.

nodes.name: Salome II (Daughter of Herod I & Elpis, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.role: Daughter of Herod I & Elpis
nodes.notes: Youngest daughter of Herod the Great, betrothed to a son of Pheroras.

nodes.name: King Herod Agrippa I (King of All Judea 41–44 CE, Acts 12)
nodes.role: Grandson of Herod & Mariamne I Who Executed James & Imprisoned Peter
nodes.notes: Son of Aristobulus IV & Berenice I; married cousin Cypros bat Salampsio and fathered Herod Agrippa II, Berenice II, Mariamne IV, and Drusilla.

nodes.name: King Herod of Chalcis (41–48 CE, Josephus Ant. XIX–XX)
nodes.role: Grandson of Herod & Husband of Berenice II
nodes.notes: Son of Aristobulus IV & Berenice I; ruled Chalcis in Lebanon and married niece Queen Berenice II; fathered King Aristobulus of Armenia Minor.

nodes.name: Aristobulus Minor (Son of Aristobulus IV & Berenice I, Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.role: Husband of Iotape of Emesa
nodes.notes: Younger brother of Herod Agrippa I; wed Princess Iotape of Emesa and fathered deaf-mute daughter Iotape.

nodes.name: Princess Herodias (Daughter of Aristobulus IV & Berenice I; Matt 14:3)
nodes.era: c. 15 BCE – after 39 CE (Matt 14:3–11; Josephus Ant. XVIII.5)
nodes.role: Granddaughter of Herod & Mother of Princess Salome
nodes.notes: Married uncle Herod II (fathering Salome) and later uncle Tetrarch Herod Antipas; followed Antipas into exile in Gaul.

nodes.name: Princess Salome (Daughter of Herod II & Herodias; Queen of Chalcis & Armenia Minor)
nodes.role: Daughter of Herodias Married to Philip II & Aristobulus of Chalcis
nodes.notes: Famous dancer of Mark 6; married Tetrarch Philip II and later cousin Aristobulus of Chalcis (King of Armenia Minor), bearing Herod, Agrippa & Aristobulus.

nodes.name: King Aristobulus of Armenia Minor (Son of Herod of Chalcis; Husband of Salome, d. 92 CE)
nodes.era: c. 35–92 CE (Josephus Ant. XX.8.4; Tacitus Annals XIII.7)
nodes.role: Herodian King of Lesser Armenia Under Nero
nodes.notes: Son of Herod of Chalcis and Mariamne; appointed King of Armenia Minor by Nero and wed Princess Salome.

nodes.name: King Herod Agrippa II (Last Herodian King, c. 50–93/100 CE; Acts 25–26)
nodes.role: Last Sovereign of the Herodian Dynasty Who Heard Apostle Paul
nodes.notes: Son of Herod Agrippa I & Cypros; ruled northern territories until the Flavian era; heard Paul's defense at Caesarea.

nodes.name: Queen Berenice II (Daughter of Agrippa I; Consort of Chalcis, Pontus & Emperor Titus)
nodes.era: 28–after 79 CE (Acts 25:13; Josephus Ant. XX.7; Tacitus Hist. II)
nodes.role: Herodian Queen Married to Polemon II of Pontus & Courted by Emperor Titus
nodes.notes: Eldest daughter of Herod Agrippa I; married Marcus Julius Alexander, Herod of Chalcis, King Polemon II of Pontus/Cilicia, and famously lived with Roman general/Emperor Titus.

nodes.name: Princess Drusilla (Daughter of Agrippa I; Wife of Azizus & Felix, Acts 24:24)
nodes.role: Herodian Princess Who Perished at Pompeii (79 CE)
nodes.notes: Youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I; married King Azizus of Emesa and later Roman Procurator Antonius Felix, bearing son Agrippa.

nodes.name: Antonius Felix (Roman Procurator of Judea 52–60 CE; Husband of Drusilla, Acts 24)
nodes.role: Roman Imperial Freedmen Governor Allied by Marriage to Herod's House
nodes.notes: Roman Procurator of Judea who married Herodian princess Drusilla and examined Apostle Paul at Caesarea.

nodes.name: Agrippa (Son of Drusilla & Felix, d. 79 CE Vesuvius, Josephus Ant. XX.7.2)
nodes.role: Great-Grandson of Herod the Great Slain in the Eruption of Mt. Vesuvius
nodes.notes: Josephus records that Drusilla and Felix's young son Agrippa perished together with his wife in the 79 CE eruption of Mount Vesuvius!

nodes.name: Mariamne IV (Daughter of Herod Agrippa I; Mother of Berenice of Alexandria)
nodes.role: Herodian Princess Married to Julius Archelaus & Demetrius of Alexandria
nodes.notes: Daughter of Herod Agrippa I; wed Julius Archelaus and later alabarch Demetrius of Alexandria.

nodes.name: Saint Anne (Mother of the Virgin Mary, Protoevangelium of James)
nodes.role: Maternal Grandmother of Jesus
nodes.notes: Wife of Joachim/Heli and mother of Mary of Nazareth.

nodes.name: Sobe (Sister of Saint Anne; Mother of Elizabeth, Early Tradition)
nodes.role: Sister of Saint Anne & Grandmother of John the Baptist
nodes.notes: Early Christian tradition names Sobe sister of Saint Anne and mother of Elizabeth (kinswoman of Mary).

nodes.name: Salome (Wife of Zebedee; Mother of James & John, Matt 27:56; Mark 15:40)
nodes.role: Galilean Disciple at the Cross & Empty Tomb
nodes.notes: Wife of Zebedee and mother of Apostles James the Great and John the Evangelist.

nodes.name: Mary of Clopas (Wife of Clopas/Alphaeus, John 19:25)
nodes.role: Kinswoman at the Cross & Mother of James the Lesser & Simeon
nodes.notes: Wife of Clopas (Joseph's brother per Hegesippus) and mother of James the Lesser, Joses, and Bishop Simeon of Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Bishop Simeon of Jerusalem (Son of Clopas & Mary; 2nd Bishop, Eusebius HE III.11)
nodes.role: Cousin of Jesus & Successor to James the Just
nodes.notes: Son of Joseph's brother Clopas; elected 2nd Bishop of Jerusalem after James the Just and martyred under Trajan.

nodes.name: Apostle Simon Peter / Cephas (Son of Jonah)
nodes.role: Chief Apostle
nodes.notes: Galilean fisherman of Bethsaida; brother of Andrew.

nodes.name: Apostle Andrew (Son of Jonah; Brother of Simon Peter)
nodes.role: First-Called Apostle
nodes.notes: Brother of Simon Peter; first disciple called beside Jordan.

nodes.name: Apostle James the Great (Son of Zebedee & Salome, d. 44 CE)
nodes.role: Inner-Circle Apostle Martyred by Herod Agrippa I
nodes.notes: Elder son of Zebedee and Salome; beheaded by King Herod Agrippa I.

nodes.name: Apostle John the Evangelist (Son of Zebedee & Salome)
nodes.role: Beloved Disciple & Evangelist
nodes.notes: Younger son of Zebedee and Salome.

nodes.name: Apostle Philip of Bethsaida
nodes.role: One of the Twelve Apostles
nodes.notes: Of Bethsaida in Galilee; brought Nathanael to Jesus.

nodes.name: Apostle Bartholomew / Nathanael of Cana
nodes.role: One of the Twelve Apostles
nodes.notes: Native of Cana in Galilee.

nodes.name: Apostle Matthew / Levi (Son of Alphaeus, Mark 2:14)
nodes.role: Tax Collector of Capernaum & First Evangelist
nodes.notes: Son of Alphaeus; called from Capernaum tax booth.

nodes.name: Apostle Thomas Didymus ('The Twin')
nodes.role: Apostle Credited With Missions to Parthia & India
nodes.notes: Called Didymus ('Twin'); traditional apostle to India's Malabar Coast.

nodes.name: Apostle James the Lesser (Son of Alphaeus / Clopas, Matt 10:3)
nodes.role: One of the Twelve Apostles
nodes.notes: Son of Alphaeus/Clopas and Mary of Clopas.

nodes.name: Apostle Jude Thaddeus / Lebbaeus (Luke 6:16)
nodes.role: One of the Twelve Apostles
nodes.notes: Named Judas of James in Luke 6:16 and Thaddeus in Matthew/Mark.

nodes.name: Apostle Simon the Zealot (Kananaios, Luke 6:15)
nodes.role: One of the Twelve Apostles
nodes.notes: Zealot partisan among the Twelve.

nodes.name: Judas Iscariot (Son of Simon Iscariot, John 6:71)
nodes.role: Betrayer of Jesus Among the Twelve
nodes.notes: Son of Simon Iscariot.

nodes.name: Apostle Matthias (Chosen to Replace Judas, Acts 1:23–26)
nodes.role: Twelfth Apostle Elected After the Ascension
nodes.notes: Eyewitness chosen by lot alongside Joseph Barsabbas.

nodes.name: James the Just (Brother of the Lord; 1st Bishop of Jerusalem, d. 62 CE)
nodes.role: First Overseer of Jerusalem & Author of Epistle of James
nodes.notes: Brother/kinsman of Jesus; presided over Jerusalem Council and was martyred under Ananus II in 62 CE.

nodes.name: Jude (Brother of James & Jesus; Author of Epistle of Jude)
nodes.role: Kinsman of Jesus & NT Epistle Author
nodes.notes: His grandsons Zoker and James were summoned before Emperor Domitian as Davidic descendants (Hegesippus in Eusebius HE III.20).

nodes.name: Mary Magdalene (of Magdala, Luke 8:2; John 20)
nodes.role: First Witness of the Resurrection
nodes.notes: Galilean disciple of Magdala.

nodes.name: Joseph of Arimathea (Sanhedrin Councillor, Mark 15:43)
nodes.role: Arimathean Councillor Who Provided Jesus's Tomb
nodes.notes: Provided his rock-cut tomb for Jesus's burial.

nodes.name: Nicodemus (Pharisee & Sanhedrin Ruler, John 3, 7, 19:39)
nodes.role: Member of the Sanhedrin & Disciple
nodes.notes: Visited Jesus by night and assisted Joseph of Arimathea in Jesus's burial.

nodes.name: Lazarus of Bethany (Brother of Martha & Mary, John 11)
nodes.role: Friend Raised from the Tomb at Bethany
nodes.notes: Brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany.

nodes.name: Martha of Bethany (Sister of Lazarus & Mary, Luke 10:38; John 11)
nodes.role: Confessor of the Messiah at Bethany
nodes.notes: Elder sister and hostess of Bethany household.

nodes.name: Mary of Bethany (Sister of Lazarus & Martha, John 12:3)
nodes.role: Devoted Disciple Who Anointed Jesus at Bethany
nodes.notes: Younger sister of Lazarus and Martha.

nodes.name: Barnabas / Joseph the Levite (Cyprus; Cousin of John Mark, Acts 4:36)
nodes.role: Cypriot Levite & Companion of Apostle Paul
nodes.notes: Cypriot Levite and cousin of John Mark.

nodes.name: John Mark (Son of Mary of Jerusalem; Evangelist of Mark)
nodes.role: Author of Gospel of Mark & Founder of Alexandrian Church Tradition
nodes.notes: Son of Mary of Jerusalem and cousin of Barnabas.

nodes.name: Luke the Physician & Evangelist (Author of Luke–Acts)
nodes.role: Companion of Paul & Gentile Historian
nodes.notes: Physician and historian of the early church.

nodes.name: Lois (Grandmother of Timothy, 2 Tim 1:5)
nodes.role: Jewish Matriarch in Lycaonia & Grandmother of Timothy
nodes.notes: Commended by Paul for sincere faith passed to daughter Eunice and grandson Timothy.

nodes.name: Eunice (Daughter of Lois; Mother of Timothy, Acts 16:1; 2 Tim 1:5)
nodes.role: Jewish Mother of Bishop Timothy of Ephesus
nodes.notes: Married a Greek citizen of Lystra and raised Timothy in the Scriptures.

nodes.name: Timothy of Lystra (Son of Eunice; Co-Worker of Paul, Acts 16:1)
nodes.role: Apostolic Delegate & First Bishop of Ephesus
nodes.notes: Son of Eunice and grandson of Lois; Paul's trusted delegate to Thessalonica, Corinth, and Ephesus.

nodes.name: High Priest Menelaus (Benj. / Bilgah, 172–162 BCE, Dutripon #50)
nodes.role: Seleucid-Appointed High Priest
nodes.notes: Outbid Jason; murdered Onias III; executed at Beroea.

nodes.name: Deputy High Priest Lysimachus (Brother of Menelaus, 2 Macc 4:29)
nodes.role: Acting High Priest & Brother of Menelaus
nodes.notes: Brother of Menelaus slain during temple-treasury riot.

nodes.name: High Priest Alcimus / Jakim (162–159 BCE, 1 Macc 7; Dutripon #53)
nodes.role: Aaronic Opponent of the Maccabees
nodes.notes: Descendant of Aaron installed by Demetrius I.

nodes.name: High Priest Ananelus of Babylon (Herod's 1st Appointee, 37–36 BCE, #63)
nodes.role: High Priest Appointed by Herod I
nodes.notes: Babylonian Aaronic priest appointed twice by Herod I.

nodes.name: High Priest Jesus ben Phabet (c. 30–23 BCE, Dutripon #65)
nodes.era: c. 30–23 BCE (Josephus Ant. XV.9.3; Dutripon p. 23)
nodes.role: High Priest Under Herod I
nodes.notes: Succeeded Joshua ben Fabus; replaced by Simon ben Boethus.

nodes.name: High Priest Simon ben Boethus (23–5 BCE, #66; Father of Mariamne II)
nodes.role: Alexandrian High Priest & Father-in-Law of Herod I
nodes.notes: Father of Herod's wife Mariamne II.

nodes.name: High Priest Matthias ben Theophilus I (5–4 BCE, #67)
nodes.role: High Priest at Birth of Jesus
nodes.notes: Appointed by Herod in his final year.

nodes.name: High Priest Joazar ben Boethus (4 BCE & 6 CE, #68)
nodes.era: 4 BCE – 6 CE (Josephus Ant. XVII.6.4, XVIII.1.1; Dutripon p. 23)
nodes.role: Son of Simon ben Boethus
nodes.notes: Son of Simon ben Boethus who assisted Quirinius's 6 CE census.

nodes.name: High Priest Eleazar ben Boethus (4 BCE, #69)
nodes.role: Son of Simon ben Boethus
nodes.notes: Appointed by Archelaus after deposing his brother Joazar.

nodes.name: High Priest Jesus ben Sie (c. 4 BCE–6 CE, Dutripon #70)
nodes.role: High Priest Under Archelaus
nodes.notes: Replaced Eleazar ben Boethus.

nodes.name: Ananus I / High Priest Annas (6–15 CE, #72; Father of 5 High Priests!)
nodes.era: 6–15 CE (Luke 3:2; John 18:13; Josephus Ant. XVIII.2, XX.9.1)
nodes.role: Patriarch of the House of Annas
nodes.notes: All FIVE of his sons (Eleazar, Jonathan, Theophilus, Matthias, Ananus II) plus his son-in-law Joseph Caiaphas served as High Priest!

nodes.name: High Priest Ishmael ben Fabus (15–16 CE, Dutripon #73)
nodes.role: Roman-Era High Priest
nodes.notes: Appointed by Prefect Valerius Gratus.

nodes.name: High Priest Eleazar ben Ananus (16–17 CE, Son 1 of Annas)
nodes.role: Eldest Son of High Priest Annas
nodes.notes: First of Annas's five sons to hold the High Priesthood.

nodes.name: High Priest Simon ben Camithus (17–18 CE)
nodes.role: Predecessor of Caiaphas
nodes.notes: Served one year immediately preceding Joseph Caiaphas.

nodes.name: High Priest Joseph Caiaphas (18–36 CE; Son-in-Law of Annas, Trial of Jesus)
nodes.role: High Priest at Crucifixion of Jesus
nodes.notes: Married Annas's daughter and presided over the Sanhedrin trial of Jesus.

nodes.name: High Priest Jonathan ben Ananus (36–37 CE, Son 2 of Annas)
nodes.era: 36–37 CE, d. 56 CE (Josephus Ant. XVIII.4.3, XX.8.5)
nodes.role: Second Son of High Priest Annas
nodes.notes: Succeeded brother-in-law Caiaphas; later assassinated by Sicarii.

nodes.name: High Priest Theophilus ben Ananus (37–41 CE, Son 3 of Annas)
nodes.role: Third Son of High Priest Annas
nodes.notes: Third son of Annas; father of High Priest Matthias ben Theophilus.

nodes.name: High Priest Simon Cantheras ben Boethus (41–43 CE)
nodes.role: Boethusian Son of Simon ben Boethus
nodes.notes: Appointed by King Herod Agrippa I.

nodes.name: High Priest Matthias ben Ananus (43 CE, Son 4 of Annas)
nodes.role: Fourth Son of High Priest Annas
nodes.notes: Fourth of Annas's five sons to hold the office.

nodes.name: High Priest Elioneus ben Cantheras (44–45 CE)
nodes.role: Son of Simon Cantheras
nodes.notes: Son of Simon Cantheras; appointed by Herod Agrippa I.

nodes.name: High Priest Joseph ben Camydus / Cami (45–47 CE)
nodes.role: Appointed by Herod of Chalcis
nodes.notes: Served two years under Herod of Chalcis.

nodes.name: High Priest Ananias ben Nebedeus (47–59 CE, Trial of Paul, Acts 23:2)
nodes.role: Presided at Trial of Apostle Paul
nodes.notes: Presided over Paul's Sanhedrin examination (Acts 23); assassinated in 66 CE.

nodes.name: High Priest Ananus II ben Ananus (62 CE, Son 5 of Annas; Executed James the Just)
nodes.role: Fifth Son of Annas Who Convened Sanhedrin Against James
nodes.notes: Youngest of Annas's five sons; ordered the execution of James the Just in 62 CE and later led moderate Jerusalem defense.

nodes.name: High Priest Jesus ben Damneus (62–63 CE)
nodes.role: Appointed After Ananus II
nodes.notes: Succeeded Ananus II upon King Agrippa II's intervention.

nodes.name: High Priest Jesus ben Gamaliel (+ Martha bat Boethus, 63–65 CE)
nodes.role: High Priest & Educator Remembered in Talmud Yevamot 61a
nodes.notes: Married wealthy Martha of Boethus; slain alongside Ananus II in 68 CE.

nodes.name: High Priest Matthias ben Theophilus (65–68 CE, Grandson of Annas)
nodes.role: Last Regularly Appointed High Priest of Jerusalem
nodes.notes: Son of Theophilus ben Ananus and grandson of High Priest Annas.

nodes.name: High Priest Phannias / Phanacius ben Samuel (Last High Priest, 70 CE Siege)
nodes.role: Final High Priest of the Second Temple (Chosen by Lot)
nodes.notes: Simple village Aaronic priest chosen by lot during the Zealot siege; last High Priest before the 70 CE destruction.

nodes.name: Tobiel (Grandfather of Tobias, Tribe of Naphtali; Tobit 1:1)
nodes.role: Father of Tobit
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Tobit in the Tribe of Naphtali (descended from Ananiel -> Aduel -> Gabael -> Raphael -> Raguel -> Asiel -> Jahzeel).

nodes.name: Tobit (+ Wife Anna; Exiled to Nineveh Under Shalmaneser, Tobit 1)
nodes.role: Righteous Naphtalite Exile in Nineveh
nodes.notes: Father of Tobias; nephew Ahiqar served as royal cupbearer in Nineveh.

nodes.name: Tobias (Son of Tobit & Anna; Husband of Sarah bat Raguel, Tobit 6–8)
nodes.role: Son of Tobit
nodes.notes: Journeyed to Rages/Ecbatana in Media and married cousin Sarah.

nodes.name: Raguel (+ Wife Edna; Kinsmen at Ecbatana, Tobit 7:2)
nodes.role: Parents of Sarah Wife of Tobias
nodes.notes: Pious Naphtalite relatives of Tobit residing in Ecbatana.

nodes.name: Sarah (Daughter of Raguel & Edna; Wife of Tobias, Tobit 3:7)
nodes.role: Wife of Tobias
nodes.notes: Daughter of Raguel and Edna who bore seven sons to Tobias.

nodes.name: Judith of Bethulia (Widow of Manasseh; Simeon's Line, Judith 8:1–2)
nodes.role: Deliverer of Bethulia From Holofernes
nodes.notes: Judith 8:1 gives her full 16-generation genealogy through Merari, Ox, Joseph, Oziel, Elkiah, Ananias, Gideon, Raphaim, Ahitub, Elihu, Eliab, Nathanael, Salamiel, Sarasadai back to Simeon!

nodes.name: General Holofernes (Assyrian Commander Under Nebuchadnezzar, Judith 2)
nodes.role: Commander Slain by Judith of Bethulia
nodes.notes: Chief general slain by Judith at the siege of Bethulia.

nodes.name: Susanna (Daughter of Hilkiah; Wife of Joakim in Babylon, Dan 13)
nodes.role: Righteous Woman Vindicated by Young Daniel
nodes.notes: Daughter of Hilkiah and wife of prominent exile Joakim in Babylon.

nodes.name: Eleazar the Aged Scribe (90-Year-Old Martyr, 2 Macc 6:18)
nodes.role: Principal Scribe Martyred Under Antiochus IV
nodes.notes: 90-year-old scribe who refused to eat swine's flesh under Antiochus IV Epiphanes.

nodes.name: Hannah / Solomonia & Her Seven Maccabean Martyr Sons (2 Macc 7; 4 Macc 15)
nodes.role: Mother of the Seven Maccabean Martyrs
nodes.notes: Mother whose seven sons suffered martyrdom in defense of Torah.

nodes.name: Jesus ben Eleazar ben Sira (Ben Sira, Author of Ecclesiasticus, c. 180 BCE)
nodes.role: Sage of Jerusalem & Author of Sirach
nodes.notes: Grandson translated his Hebrew wisdom scroll into Greek in Alexandria c. 132 BCE.

nodes.name: Dositheus (Priest/Levite Carrier of Greek Esther to Egypt, Esth 11:1 LXX)
nodes.role: Carrier of the Purim Letter With Son Ptolemy
nodes.notes: With his son Ptolemy brought the Phrurai (Purim) letter to Egypt in the 4th year of Ptolemy & Cleopatra.

nodes.name: Prophetess Huldah (Wife of Shallum ben Tikvah, 2 Kgs 22:14)
nodes.role: Court Prophetess of King Josiah
nodes.notes: Authenticated the newly discovered Book of the Law for King Josiah.

nodes.name: Prophetess Anna bat Phanuel (Tribe of Asher, Luke 2:36)
nodes.role: 84-Year-Old Asherite Prophetess in the Temple
nodes.notes: Daughter of Phanuel of the Tribe of Asher who recognized infant Jesus in the Temple.

nodes.name: Chedorlaomer, King of Elam (Gen 14:1–17)
nodes.role: Elamite Suzerain Defeated by Abraham
nodes.notes: King of Elam leading four Mesopotamian kings against Sodom before Abraham rescued Lot.

nodes.name: King Sihon of the Amorites (Heshbon, Num 21:21–31)
nodes.role: Amorite King of Heshbon
nodes.notes: Ruled central Transjordan from the Arnon to the Jabbok.

nodes.name: King Og of Bashan (Last of the Rephaim Giants, Deut 3:11)
nodes.role: Amorite-Rephaim King of Ashtaroth & Edrei
nodes.notes: King of Bashan remembered for his nine-cubit iron bedstead at Rabbah.

nodes.name: King Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram-Naharaim (Judg 3:8)
nodes.role: First Foreign Oppressor in Judges
nodes.notes: Oppressed Israel 8 years until defeated by 1st Judge Othniel.

nodes.name: King Eglon of Moab (Judges 3:12–25)
nodes.role: Moabite King Slain by Judge Ehud
nodes.notes: Captured Jericho ('City of Palms') before Judge Ehud slew him.

nodes.name: King Jabin of Hazor (Judges 4:2)
nodes.role: Canaanite King of Northern Hazor
nodes.notes: Ruled Hazor with 900 iron chariots under commander Sisera.

nodes.name: General Sisera of Harosheth-hagoyim (Judges 4:2–22)
nodes.role: Canaanite Commander Slain by Jael
nodes.notes: Routed by Deborah & Barak at Kishon and slain by Jael wife of Heber the Kenite.

nodes.name: Zerah the Cushite / Ethiopian (2 Chr 14:9)
nodes.role: Cushite Invader Defeated by King Asa
nodes.notes: Marched against Judah at Mareshah before King Asa routed his host.

nodes.name: King Tibni ben Ginath of Israel (Rival of Omri, 1 Kgs 16:21–22)
nodes.role: Co-Regnant Northern Rival of Omri
nodes.notes: Backed by half of Northern Israel for four years against Omri.
